name: LoFTR
plain: LoFTR (Zhejiang University, CVPR 2021): detector-free matching of two photos of one scene with transformers; semi-dense matches as keypoint pairs (the form COLMAP takes). Outdoor (MegaDepth) and indoor (ScanNet) weights. Apache-2.0 code and weights.
summary: LoFTR (Sun et al., CVPR 2021): detector-free dense matching. A ResNet-FPN gives 1/8 and 1/2 resolution features; a linear-attention transformer matches the 1/8 cells of both images (dual-softmax, mutual nearest neighbours above a confidence threshold) and a second transformer refines each match to sub-pixel precision in a 5 x 5 window at 1/2 resolution. Returns the matched points of both images, their (identity) index pairs and the coarse confidence.

papers.title: LoFTR: Detector-Free Local Feature Matching with Transformers

no_kernels_reason: not implemented yet: data-dependent match counts (mutual nearest neighbours above a threshold)
limitations: Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; every match is its own keypoint pair (`pairs` is `[[0, 0], [1, 1], ...]`).
One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the match counts differ per pair.
No exportable module: the match counts are data-dependent (`torch.compile` runs with graph breaks; ONNX / TensorRT export fails).

Images are converted to grayscale and matched at `long_side` (default 840, upstream's MegaDepth test size); the coarse matching holds an (H W / 64)^2 score matrix, so memory grows with the 4th power of the side. The indoor weights were evaluated by upstream at 640 x 480 (ScanNet).
task_io: Input: two RGB images of one scene. Output: for every pixel of the first image its position in the second (x, y in pixels) and a certainty that the pixel is visible in both. Sparse matchers (LightGlue) return the keypoints of both images and the index pairs of the matched ones instead.

quality.title: MegaDepth-1500, every 10th pair, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees
quality.protocol: Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors.
